Zainab and I collaborated on two projects at FinTech Innovators, where she handled model deployment and infrastructure scaling. She’s the kind of engineer who asks, “What’s the next bottleneck?” and then builds a pipeline to solve it.  

Daily, she manages AWS EC2 clusters for training, trimming costs by 18% through spot instance optimizations. Her Dockerized models cut deployment time by 40%, and she’s the go-to person for Kubernetes issues—once she fixed a scaling outage that had the team stuck for 12 hours. She’ll often say, “Let’s just try PyTorch for this,” then methodically debugs TensorFlow issues others overlook. Her NLP work on customer sentiment analysis boosted classifier accuracy to 92%, which directly impacted churn metrics.  

A standout was her LLM-based fraud detection system. She iterated prompts for 3 weeks, fine-tuning a model to flag 23% more suspicious transactions without false positives. She also spearheaded MLOps upgrades, replacing legacy scripts with Airflow workflows that reduced manual intervention by 70%.  

Zainab’s strength lies in her quiet reliability—she’ll stay late to troubleshoot a pipeline or refactor code others avoid. Her technical depth and obsession with measurable outcomes make her a rare asset. I’d trust her to ship complex systems under pressure, and she’d do it with minimal fanfare.
